extraction.summary: Theo Bergstrom, a 74-year-old male with a history of CKD stage 3b, prostate cancer, and recurrent UTIs, presented to the ED via ambulance with confusion, slurred speech, and reduced oral intake. Initial observations demonstrated high fever (38.9°C), tachycardia (124 bpm), tachypnea (28/min), hypotension (88/52 mmHg), hypoxia (90% on 6 L/min O2), altered mental state (AVPU V), poor peripheral perfusion, and severe oliguria (15 mL/hr). Bedside blood testing revealed critical hyperlactatemia (4.8 mmol/L), severe leukocytosis (WBC 17.2 x10^9/L), elevated CRP (187 mg/L), and acute renal failure (Creatinine 218 umol/L). Sepsis Six protocols have been initiated, medical registrar and critical care outreach teams have been alerted, and CT imaging has been requested.
extraction.clinical_reasoning: The patient's presentation and constellation of vital signs and laboratory findings are consistent with septic shock, most likely secondary to urosepsis given his history of recurrent UTIs and prostate cancer. Major drivers of clinical concern include systemic hypotension (BP 88/52 mmHg), tachycardia (124 bpm), tachypnea (28/min), fever (38.9°C), hypoxia on supplemental oxygen, altered mental state (AVPU V), delayed capillary refill (4 seconds), oliguria (15 mL output in first hour), critically elevated lactate (4.8 mmol/L), severe inflammatory markers (WBC 17.2 x10^9/L, CRP 187 mg/L), and acute renal injury (Creatinine 218 umol/L, Urea 19.4 mmol/L) on background CKD.
recommended_next_steps: Immediate bedside evaluation by the bleeped medical registrar and critical care outreach team.
Re-evaluate hemodynamic response and fluid balance post 500 mL Hartmann's bolus, anticipating requirement for further IV fluid resuscitation or vasopressor support.
Perform requested CT abdomen/pelvis once stabilized.
Maintain strict hourly urinary output monitoring via catheter.
Follow up pending formal laboratory bloods, formal blood cultures, and repeat lactate levels.
